    The Artemis II mission uses the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket, which stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall when fully stacked with the Orion spacecraft. This height makes it taller than the Statue of Liberty and comparable to a 30-story building. 
    • Total Height: 322 feet (
      ).
    • Rocket Components: The SLS rocket itself, including boosters, is ~322 ft.
    • Comparison: The rocket is about 7 feet taller than London's Big Ben. 
    The Artemis II crew, consisting of four astronauts, launched from NASA's Kennedy Space Center aboard this vehicle for a 10-day mission around the Moon.

    How long will Artemis 2 take to get to the Moon?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The
    Artemis II Orion spacecraft will take approximately five to six days to reach the vicinity of the Moon. The crew will fly around the far side of the Moon on day six before returning, with the entire mission lasting roughly 10 days. 
    Key Mission Details: 
    • Duration to Moon: The crew will reach their closest point to the Moon on the 6th day of the mission.
    • Total Mission Length: The trip is planned as a 10-day, or nine-day, one-hour, and 46-minute, mission.
    • Distance: The crew will travel about 252,000 miles, passing 4,000 to 5,000 miles beyond the far side of the Moon
      .
    • Mission Goal: This is a test flight, rather than a landing mission, setting records for the farthest humans have ever traveled into space. 
    The mission uses a "free-return trajectory," which relies on Earth's and the Moon's gravity to guide the spacecraft around the moon and back.
